collection.description: The village cuts its grinding stones from a cliff of soft grey rock at the edge of the hills.

ask.text:
The village cuts its grinding stones from a cliff of soft grey rock at the edge of the hills. (Name) has been working there all morning, chipping out a new stone for the cooks, when (he/she) hears a crack from high above. A little shower of pebbles patters down onto (his/her) shoulders. Then a bigger one.
The cliff is letting go. (Name) has a moment, maybe two. Should (he/she) run for the open ground, or press flat against the cliff face where the overhang might protect (him/her)?

c1o1.text: (Name) almost makes it. A single stone, bouncing ahead of the rest, catches (him/her) on the side of the head and knocks (him/her) flat. The others find (him/her) lying in the open, bleeding but breathing. When (he/she) wakes in the healers' hut, (he/she) can't remember (his/her) own name. Not a syllable. Until it comes back, the village calls (him/her) "?".

c1o2.text: The rocks catch (name)'s leg just as (he/she) reaches the edge of the slide. It takes four people an hour to dig (him/her) out. The healers do what they can, but the leg never bends properly again, and (name) walks with a stick from then on. (He/She) never goes back to the quarry, and the cooks make do with the old grinding stone.

c1.text: (Name) drops (his/her) tools and runs. Behind (him/her), the roar of the falling rock grows louder and louder...

c2o1.text: The overhang gives way with the rest. When the dust settles, the quarry is a heap of grey rubble, and (name) is under it. The village digs for two days to bring (him/her) home. They bury (him/her) with the grinding stone (he/she) was cutting, finished by the other quarry workers, set at the head of the grave.

c2o2.text: The overhang holds. The rocks pile up on every side, but (name) is left in a little pocket of space under the cliff, covered in dust, coughing, completely unhurt. It takes the village half a day to dig (him/her) out. (He/She) comes out holding the grinding stone, which is also unhurt. "I finished it," (he/she) says. "In the dark."

c2.text: (Name) throws (himself/herself) against the cliff face under the overhang, arms over (his/her) head. The world goes dark with dust and noise...
